claims.claim: The WikiProject records that the significance-inflating statements appear even for the most mundane subjects such as etymology or population data.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs may even include these statements for even the most mundane of subjects
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends'

claims.claim: An October 2024 revision to the Wikipedia article on Kumba, Cameroon, cited by the WikiProject as an example of the tell, closes a road-network sentence with the clause that it helped solidify its role as a regional hub.
claims.source: AI-generated Wikipedia text quoted as a demonstration example by WikiProject AI Cleanup
claims.quote: helped solidify its role as a regional hub
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends', examples

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that AI chatbots insert superficial analysis of information, often about its significance, recognition or impact, typically as a trailing present-participle phrase.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: insert superficial analysis of information, often in relation to its significance

claims.claim: A June 2023 revision to the Wikipedia article on Douera, cited by the WikiProject as an example of superficial analysis, follows a census population figure with the clause creating a lively community within its borders.
claims.source: AI-generated Wikipedia text quoted as a demonstration example by WikiProject AI Cleanup
claims.quote: creating a lively community within its borders

claims.feature: other: vague attribution and weasel wording
claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that AI chatbots attribute opinions or claims to a vague authority and exaggerate the number of sources holding them.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: AI chatbots tend to attribute opinions or claims to some vague authority
claims.page: section 'Vague attributions and overgeneralization of opinions'

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that one or two AI-vocabulary words may be coincidence but a post-2022 edit introducing lots of them, lots of times, is one of the strongest tells for AI use.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: an edit (post-2022) introducing lots of them, lots of times
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'

claims.claim: The WikiProject notes that while most studies of AI vocabulary analysed scientific abstracts or fiction, those words are also ubiquitous in LLM-based encyclopedias such as Grokipedia.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: "AI vocabulary" words are also ubiquitous in LLM-based encyclopedias
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'

claims.claim: The WikiProject records that delve was famously overused by ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024, became less frequent later in 2024 and dropped off sharply in 2025.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: the word delve was famously overused by ChatGPT in 2023
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'

claims.claim: The WikiProject gives three era word-lists, assigning Additionally, boasts, delve, intricate, tapestry and testament to GPT-4 in 2023 to mid-2024, and only emphasizing, enhance, highlighting and showcasing to GPT-5 from mid-2025.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: The words that LLMs overuse have changed over time.
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words', era breakdown

claims.claim: The WikiProject records Grok as idiosyncratic in overusing superficially scientific words such as causal, empirical and correlate, and in still overusing underscore as of 2026.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLM text replaces copulas such as is or are with constructions like serves as, stands as, marks, features and offers.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: replaces simple constructions that use copulas such as is or are

claims.claim: The WikiProject cites a study documenting an over 10% decrease in the usage of the words is and are in academic writing in 2023, with no major change before that.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup relaying a cited study, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: decrease in the usage of the words is and are

claims.feature: other: vague connection instead of a stated relation
claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLMs allude vaguely to two subjects being connected to or associated with each other instead of stating the relation directly.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs will often allude vaguely to the two subjects being
claims.page: section 'Vague expression of connection or association'

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLMs overuse the rule of three, in the form adjective-adjective-adjective or three short phrases.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs overuse the rule of three

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that LLMs use the rule of three to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs often use this structure to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs may even include these statements for even the most mundane of subjects like etymology or population data.
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext of the live 6 Sep 2026 revision (revid 1373524112, action=raw, 220246 bytes). Line 69, inside section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends' (heading at line 39, next heading line 88). Quote appears word for word; 'these statements' refers back to the puffery statements about importance, and 'etymology or population data' is on the page verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: The establishment of road networks ... helped solidify its role as a regional hub.
verdicts.note: Line 51-52: collapse box labelled 'From [[Special:Diff/1248482444|this October 2024 revision]] to [[Kumba, Cameroon]]', under the 'Examples' of the 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends' section. Sentence reads 'The establishment of road networks connecting Kumba to other parts of the Southwest Region, such as Mamfe and Buea, helped {{highlight|solidify its role as a regional hub}}.' Every limb (Oct 2024 revision, Kumba Cameroon, cited as an example, road-network sentence, closing clause) checks out; the {{highlight}} markup is rendering, not text.

verdicts.trueWording: AI chatbots tend to insert superficial analysis of information, often in relation to its significance, recognition, or impact.
verdicts.note: Line 132, section 'Superficial analyses' (heading line 129). Quote verbatim. The participle limb is supported by the next sentence: 'This is often done by attaching a present participle ("-ing") phrase at the end of sentences' — the claim's 'typically' is a shade stronger than the page's 'often', but names the same pattern.

verdicts.trueWording: the population of Douera stood at approximately 56,998 inhabitants, creating a lively community within its borders.
verdicts.note: Line 138-140, section 'Superficial analyses', examples box labelled '2023-2025', attributed 'From this June 2023 revision to [[Douéra]]' (diff 1161677884). Quote verbatim; it does follow the April 2008 census population figure. Only cosmetic gap: the article title on the page is accented 'Douéra' while the quoted AI text itself spells it 'Douera' as the claim does.

verdicts.trueWording: AI chatbots tend to attribute opinions or claims to some vague authority—a practice called weasel wording.
verdicts.note: Line 227, section 'Vague attributions and overgeneralization of opinions' (heading line 223). Quote verbatim, and the second limb is the following sentence: 'They also commonly exaggerate the quantity of sources that these opinions are attributed to.'

verdicts.trueWording: One or two ... may be coincidental, but an edit (post-2022) introducing lots of them, lots of times, is one of the strongest tells for AI use.
verdicts.note: Line 330, section 'High density of "AI vocabulary" words' (heading line 325). Quote verbatim and both limbs (coincidence vs strongest tell) present in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: While most of these studies have analyzed scientific abstracts or fiction, "AI vocabulary" words are also ubiquitous in LLM-based encyclopedias, such as Grokipedia
verdicts.note: Line 330, same paragraph. Quote verbatim including the quotation marks around 'AI vocabulary'. Grokipedia is named as the example; the page adds 'and in AI-generated Wikipedia text', which the claim omits but does not contradict.

verdicts.trueWording: the word delve was famously overused by ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024, but became less frequent later in 2024, then dropped off sharply in 2025.
verdicts.note: Line 332, section 'High density of "AI vocabulary" words'. Rendered text matches the quote word for word ('delve' is wikilinked/italicised in wikitext only). All three limbs — 2023/early 2024 overuse, decline later in 2024, sharp drop in 2025 — are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Mid-2025 and on (GPT-5): emphasizing, enhance, highlighting, showcasing (plus words associated with 'Canned emphasis on notability...')
verdicts.note: Quote 'The words that LLMs overuse have changed over time.' is verbatim at line 332 and there are exactly three era bullets (2023 to mid-2024 / GPT-4; Mid-2024 to mid-2025 / GPT-4o; Mid-2025 and on / GPT-5). All six words named for the GPT-4 era (Additionally, boasts, delve, intricate/intricacies, tapestry, testament) are in that bullet. The failing limb is the word 'only' on the GPT-5 bullet: the page's GPT-5 line is not closed at four words — it ends with a parenthetical adding the whole word-set of the 'Canned emphasis on notability, attribution, and media coverage' section.

verdicts.trueWording: Grok output is particularly idiosyncratic: it overuses superficially "scientific" words like causal, empirical, correlate, and continues to overuse underscore as of 2026.
verdicts.note: Line 338, section 'High density of "AI vocabulary" words'. Quote verbatim; both limbs (the three scientific words, and continued underscore overuse as of 2026) are in the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: LLM-generated text often replaces simple constructions that use copulas such as is or are with constructions such as serves as a or mark the.
verdicts.note: Line 378, section 'Avoidance of basic copulatives ("is"/"are" phrases)' (heading line 374). Quote verbatim. Every listed substitute is on the page: the section's words-to-watch box (line 376) reads 'serves as/stands as/marks/functions as/operates as/represents [a], boasts/features/maintains/offers [a], refers to', and the body adds 'marketing-related verbs like features, offers'.

verdicts.trueWording: One study documented an over 10% decrease in the usage of the words is and are in academic writing in 2023, with no major changes in their frequency before that.
verdicts.note: Line 378, same section; the study cited is Geng & Trotta, 'Is ChatGPT Transforming Academics' Writing Style?' (arXiv 2404.08627). Quote verbatim and both limbs (over 10% decrease in 2023; no major prior change) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs will often allude vaguely to the two subjects being "connected to" or "associated with" each other
verdicts.note: Line 397, section 'Vague expression of connection or association' (heading line 393). Quote verbatim; the 'instead of stating the relation directly' limb is the sentence opener: 'Rather than directly stating a connection or relationship between two subjects'.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs overuse the rule of three. This can take different forms, from "adjective, adjective, adjective" to "short phrase, short phrase, and short phrase".
verdicts.note: Line 503, section 'Rule of three' (heading line 501). Quote verbatim and both named forms present.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs often use this structure to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive.
verdicts.note: Line 503, section 'Rule of three', the sentence immediately after the rule-of-three forms. Quote verbatim in rendered text ('superficial analyses' carries an internal wikilink in the wikitext only).
